paragraphs.text: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? or need we, as do some, epistles of commendation to you or from you?
paragraphs.original: Ἀρχόμεθα πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνειν; ἢ μὴ χρῄζομεν ὥς τινες συστατικῶν ἐπιστολῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐξ ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: Archometha palin heautous synistanein; ē mē chrēzomen hōs tines systatikōn epistolōn pros hymas ē ex hymōn;

paragraphs.text: Ye are our epistle, written in our hearts, known and read of all men;
paragraphs.original: ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν ὑμεῖς ἐστε, ἐγγεγραμμένη ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν, γινωσκομένη καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων·
paragraphs.translit: hē epistolē hēmōn hymeis este, engegrammenē en tais kardiais hēmōn, ginōskomenē kai anaginōskomenē hypo pantōn anthrōpōn·

paragraphs.text: being made manifest that ye are an epistle of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in tables [that are] hearts of flesh.
paragraphs.original: φανερούμενοι ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφʼ ἡμῶν, ἐγγεγραμμένη οὐ μέλανι ἀλλὰ πνεύματι θεοῦ ζῶντος, οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν λιθίναις ἀλλʼ ἐν πλαξὶν καρδίαις σαρκίναις.
paragraphs.translit: phaneroumenoi hoti este epistolē Christou diakonētheisa hyphʼ hēmōn, engegrammenē ou melani alla pneumati theou zōntos, ouk en plaxin lithinais allʼ en plaxin kardiais sarkinais.

paragraphs.text: And such confidence have we through Christ to God-ward:
paragraphs.original: Πεποίθησιν δὲ τοιαύτην ἔχομεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.
paragraphs.translit: Pepoithēsin de toiautēn echomen dia tou Christou pros ton theon.

paragraphs.text: not that we are sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;
paragraphs.original: οὐχ ὅτι ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν λογίσασθαί τι ὡς ἐξ αὑτῶν, ἀλλʼ ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ouch hoti aphʼ heautōn hikanoi esmen logisasthai ti hōs ex hautōn, allʼ hē hikanotēs hēmōn ek tou theou,

paragraphs.text: who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.
paragraphs.original: ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης, οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος, τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτέννει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζῳοποιεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: hos kai hikanōsen hēmas diakonous kainēs diathēkēs, ou grammatos alla pneumatos, to gar gramma apoktennei, to de pneuma zōopoiei.

paragraphs.text: But if the ministration of death, written, [and] engraven on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look stedfastly upon the face of Moses for the glory of his face; which [glory] was passing away:
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν γράμμασιν ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον Μωϋσέως διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν καταργουμένην,
paragraphs.translit: Ei de hē diakonia tou thanatou en grammasin entetypōmenē lithois egenēthē en doxē, hōste mē dynasthai atenisai tous hyious Israēl eis to prosōpon Mōyseōs dia tēn doxan tou prosōpou autou tēn katargoumenēn,

paragraphs.text: how shall not rather the ministration of the spirit be with glory?
paragraphs.original: πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἡ διακονία τοῦ πνεύματος ἔσται ἐν δόξῃ;
paragraphs.translit: pōs ouchi mallon hē diakonia tou pneumatos estai en doxē;

paragraphs.text: For if the ministration of condemnation hath glory, much rather doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ τῇ διακονίᾳ τῆς κατακρίσεως δόξα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον περισσεύει ἡ διακονία τῆς δικαιοσύνης δόξῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar tē diakonia tēs katakriseōs doxa, pollō mallon perisseuei hē diakonia tēs dikaiosynēs doxē.

paragraphs.text: For verily that which hath been made glorious hath not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasseth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐ δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει εἵνεκεν τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης δόξης·
paragraphs.translit: kai gar ou dedoxastai to dedoxasmenon en toutō tō merei heineken tēs hyperballousēs doxēs·

paragraphs.text: For if that which passeth away [was] with glory, much more that which remaineth [is] in glory.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ τὸ καταργούμενον διὰ δόξης, πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ μένον ἐν δόξῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar to katargoumenon dia doxēs, pollō mallon to menon en doxē.

paragraphs.text: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
paragraphs.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα πολλῇ παρρησίᾳ χρώμεθα,
paragraphs.translit: Echontes oun toiautēn elpida pollē parrēsia chrōmetha,

paragraphs.text: and [are] not as Moses, [who] put a veil upon his face, that the children of Israel should not look stedfastly on the end of that which was passing away:
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐ καθάπερ Μωϋσῆς ἐτίθει κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ou kathaper Mōysēs etithei kalymma epi to prosōpon autou, pros to mē atenisai tous hyious Israēl eis to telos tou katargoumenou.

paragraphs.text: but their minds were hardened: for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remaineth, it not being revealed [to them] that it is done away in Christ.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται,
paragraphs.translit: alla epōrōthē ta noēmata autōn. achri gar tēs sēmeron hēmeras to auto kalymma epi tē anagnōsei tēs palaias diathēkēs menei mē anakalyptomenon, hoti en Christō katargeitai,

paragraphs.text: But unto this day, whensoever Moses is read, a veil lieth upon their heart.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ἕως σήμερον ἡνίκα ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται Μωϋσῆς κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν κεῖται·
paragraphs.translit: allʼ heōs sēmeron hēnika an anaginōskētai Mōysēs kalymma epi tēn kardian autōn keitai·

paragraphs.text: But whensoever it shall turn to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
paragraphs.original: ἡνίκα δὲ ἐὰν ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς κύριον, περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα.
paragraphs.translit: hēnika de ean epistrepsē pros kyrion, periaireitai to kalymma.

paragraphs.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, [there] is liberty.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν· οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου, ἐλευθερία.
paragraphs.translit: ho de kyrios to pneuma estin· hou de to pneuma kyriou, eleutheria.

paragraphs.text: But we all, with unveiled face beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord the Spirit.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν, καθάπερ ἀπὸ κυρίου πνεύματος.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de pantes anakekalymmenō prosōpō tēn doxan kyriou katoptrizomenoi tēn autēn eikona metamorphoumetha apo doxēs eis doxan, kathaper apo kyriou pneumatos.
